title: Flourishing Function Register
framing: Kapukai analytical proposal for testing whether law, norms, technology, and funding preserve human flourishing across relationships and life stages. It is not a legal standard or a claim that every institution follows the same design.
priorityRule: Priority is based on dependency and potential irreversibility, not on the moral worth of one person or relationship. Foundation functions are gating conditions; later functions must not be used to excuse a failure at an earlier gate.
highSignalLabel: ASSERTION RECEIVED · EVIDENCE STATUS: UNKNOWN · FINDING: NONE
provisionalLabel: PROVISIONAL SAFETY ACTION · BASIS RECORDED · SCOPE AND EXPIRY SHOWN · REVIEW DUE

auditStates.label: Preserved
auditStates.meaning: Evidence shows the function was supported within the defined scope.

auditStates.label: Constrained
auditStates.meaning: The function was limited; the scope, reason, duration, and review path are documented.

auditStates.label: Harm signal
auditStates.meaning: Evidence indicates a material risk or adverse effect, without claiming a system-wide finding.

auditStates.label: Unknown
auditStates.meaning: The required evidence is not available or not yet assessed.

auditStates.label: Not in scope
auditStates.meaning: The function is not part of the defined decision or relationship.

relationshipScopes.label: Person ↔ self
relationshipScopes.purpose: Body, identity, agency, privacy, meaning, and capacity to make or refuse choices.
relationshipScopes.test: Can the person understand, participate, consent where required, correct the record, and obtain help without surrendering personhood?

relationshipScopes.label: Infant / child ↔ caregiver
relationshipScopes.purpose: Safety, attachment, developmental continuity, voice, and reliable care.
relationshipScopes.test: Does the design protect the child while preserving safe relationships and giving age-appropriate voice and review?

relationshipScopes.label: Older child / adolescent
relationshipScopes.purpose: Increasing autonomy, identity formation, education, safety, and trusted support.
relationshipScopes.test: Does decision authority expand with capacity while keeping protection, privacy, and a route to challenge?

relationshipScopes.label: Partners / intimate relationships
relationshipScopes.purpose: Consent, bodily safety, reciprocity, privacy, and freedom from coercive control.
relationshipScopes.test: Are risk signals evaluated separately for each person, without treating one unverified account as a permanent finding?

relationshipScopes.label: Family / kinship group
relationshipScopes.purpose: Care continuity, belonging, conflict repair, and protection from collective punishment.
relationshipScopes.test: Does the system preserve safe care and distinguish individual conduct from family membership or association?

relationshipScopes.label: Older adult / dependent person ↔ caregiver
relationshipScopes.purpose: Dignity, supported decision-making, health, safety, and protection from neglect or exploitation.
relationshipScopes.test: Are capacity and support assessed without turning dependence into a loss of rights?

relationshipScopes.label: Peers / community / cultural group
relationshipScopes.purpose: Belonging, inclusion, mutual aid, cultural continuity, and collective voice.
relationshipScopes.test: Can the group participate and see the rules, resources, and reasons that shape its conditions?

relationshipScopes.label: Professional / service relationship
relationshipScopes.purpose: Role clarity, confidentiality, competence, fair access, and accountable handoffs.
relationshipScopes.test: Are duties, authority, conflicts, data uses, and escalation paths visible to the person receiving service?

relationshipScopes.label: Institution ↔ public
relationshipScopes.purpose: Non-arbitrary administration, reasons, transparency, equal treatment, and remedy.
relationshipScopes.test: Can a resident trace the source, authority, data, decision, funding, and correction route that affected them?

technologyLayers.name: Identity and eligibility gates
technologyLayers.examples: Identity proofing, benefits portals, DMV, eligibility engines, account recovery
technologyLayers.behavior: They decide which person or household is recognized and which services become reachable.
technologyLayers.test: Is identity provenance visible, correction possible, and uncertainty preserved rather than collapsed into denial?

technologyLayers.name: Intake and record systems
technologyLayers.examples: Court e-filing, case management, EHR, child-welfare and education records
technologyLayers.behavior: They decide what becomes a durable institutional object and what can be found later.
technologyLayers.test: Are source, author, time, version, attachments, access, and corrections preserved?

technologyLayers.name: Notification and scheduling
technologyLayers.examples: Service notices, hearing calendars, appointment systems, SMS/email portals
technologyLayers.behavior: They shape whether a person can know, attend, respond, and preserve a relationship.
technologyLayers.test: Is delivery distinct from attempted delivery, and is access context recorded without being inferred away?

technologyLayers.name: Decision support and risk flags
technologyLayers.examples: Scoring, triage queues, duplicate detection, fraud flags, recommendation tools
technologyLayers.behavior: They allocate attention and can make an unreviewed suspicion look official.
technologyLayers.test: Is the output advisory, explainable, contestable, time-limited, and separated from a factual finding?

technologyLayers.name: Funding, payment, and procurement systems
technologyLayers.examples: Appropriations, grants, contracts, reimbursements, vendor dashboards
technologyLayers.behavior: They reward what is counted, paid, reported, and closed.
technologyLayers.test: Does the metric track lived outcomes and correction capacity, or only throughput and administrative closure?

technologyLayers.name: Data exchange and analytics
technologyLayers.examples: APIs, shared identifiers, data warehouses, dashboards, data brokers
technologyLayers.behavior: They carry context across institutions and can amplify an error at scale.
technologyLayers.test: Is lineage, purpose, permission, retention, and cross-system reconciliation visible?

technologyLayers.name: Security, audit, and correction layer
technologyLayers.examples: Identity and access management, immutable logs, incident response, appeals and ticketing
technologyLayers.behavior: They determine whether a person can prove what happened and recover from an error.
technologyLayers.test: Are logs protected, accessible to authorized reviewers, and connected to a real remedy?

functions.name: Stay alive and physically safe
functions.purpose: Preserve life, bodily integrity, and freedom from preventable violence, coercion, and dangerous deprivation.
functions.minimumTest: Before an irreversible or rights-affecting action, did the system identify the risk basis, choose a proportionate protective response, record the authority, set a scope and expiry, and schedule review?
functions.relationshipTest: Does protection address the specific person and risk without treating an entire family, group, or relationship as dangerous by default?
functions.lawLens: Map emergency powers, criminal and civil protection, health and safety, child protection, elder protection, thresholds, duration, notice, review, and remedy.
functions.technologyLens: Dispatch, identity and risk flags, EHR, child-welfare systems, access control, alerts, and incident logging.
functions.fundingLens: Are prevention, response, staffing, review, and recovery funded—or only enforcement and case closure?
functions.evidence: Time-stamped source, risk facts, actor, legal authority, action, duration, notice, review result, and outcome.
failureModes: Unverified risk treated as a final fact
Protective action with no expiry or review
Throughput rewarded over actual safety

functions.name: Meet basic conditions for agency
functions.purpose: Maintain food, water, shelter, health care, medication, rest, mobility, communication, and reasonable accessibility.
functions.minimumTest: Can the person obtain the essentials needed to understand, respond, remain safe, and participate in the process?
functions.relationshipTest: Are care burdens and resource barriers visible across households, caregivers, children, elders, and people with disabilities?
functions.lawLens: Map benefits, housing, health, disability, education, labor, public-health, and accommodation duties, including eligibility and appeal rules.
functions.technologyLens: Eligibility engines, portals, payment cards, scheduling, EHR and claims systems, identity matching, and accessibility layers.
functions.fundingLens: Does funding reach prevention and direct support, or primarily administration, enforcement, and vendor volume?
functions.evidence: Eligibility inputs, notices, delivery and outage records, accommodation requests, resource availability, and appeal outcomes.
failureModes: Administrative delay becomes deprivation
Digital-only access without an equivalent path
A missing field is treated as ineligibility

functions.name: Be recognized as a person with a voice
functions.purpose: Preserve accurate identity, legal status, capacity, consent, language, disability access, and the ability to speak for oneself or through a chosen supporter.
functions.minimumTest: Can the person see what identity or status the system used, correct errors, communicate, and understand who may act for them?
functions.relationshipTest: Does representation support the person instead of silently replacing their voice or turning association into authority?
functions.lawLens: Map due process, legal identity, consent, capacity, guardianship, language access, disability accommodation, and representation rules.
functions.technologyLens: Identity proofing, account recovery, biometric or demographic matching, legal-status databases, interpreters, and portal permissions.
functions.fundingLens: Are translation, accessibility, advocacy, and correction staffed and paid as core functions?
functions.evidence: Identity provenance, consent or appointment record, capacity assessment, notices, access logs, corrections, and representative authority.
failureModes: Identity match mistaken for identity truth
Representative access without visible scope
Capacity inferred from disagreement or disability

functions.name: Maintain safe attachment and care continuity
functions.purpose: Preserve safe relationships, caregiving continuity, attachment, family connection, and stable support across life stages.
functions.minimumTest: When a relationship is restricted, is the safety basis specific, evidence-linked, proportionate, time-limited, and reviewable, with safe alternatives considered?
functions.relationshipTest: Does the system distinguish a child’s safety from a parent’s status, a partner’s allegation from a finding, and family membership from individual conduct?
functions.lawLens: Map custody, guardianship, child welfare, elder care, protection orders, visitation, placement, family preservation, and review duties.
functions.technologyLens: Child-welfare records, custody and visitation calendars, protection-order systems, placement databases, contact restrictions, and messaging systems.
functions.fundingLens: Are family preservation, kinship care, reunification, visitation support, and independent review funded alongside investigations and placements?
functions.evidence: Relationship history, safety evidence, contrary evidence, contact attempts, care plan, decision reasons, and review/repair records.
failureModes: Temporary protection becomes permanent by inertia
Placement or access decision without a traceable safety basis
Contact failure hidden as noncompliance

functions.name: Keep claims, evidence, and findings distinct
functions.purpose: Protect epistemic integrity so narratives can be heard without being mistaken for verified facts.
functions.minimumTest: For every material proposition, can a reviewer identify the source, author, time, integrity status, contrary material, challenge status, and authorized finding?
functions.relationshipTest: Can each affected person see and answer the claims that may alter their relationship, liberty, care, or resources, subject to lawful protective limits?
functions.lawLens: Map filing and intake rules, evidence standards, disclosure, confidentiality, records custody, correction routes, and judicial fact-finding.
functions.technologyLens: E-filing, OCR, metadata, hashes, docketing, search, deduplication, redaction, audit logs, and retrieval interfaces.
functions.fundingLens: Is funding tied to reliable evidence handling and correction, or to volume, speed, and closure?
functions.evidence: Source document or recording, provenance, chain of custody where relevant, version, access history, challenge, finding, and remedy.
failureModes: File accepted becomes fact found
No exhibit becomes no evidence
Narrative copied across systems without provenance

functions.name: Receive fair process and meaningful review
functions.purpose: Provide notice, understandable reasons, access, response time, impartial decision-making, accommodation, representation, and review before final deprivation.
functions.minimumTest: Did the person receive meaningful notice and a real chance to respond at a time and in a manner suited to the stakes, with a route to correction or appeal?
functions.relationshipTest: Does process protect each participant’s voice without forcing a false choice between safety and participation?
functions.lawLens: Map constitutional due process, service, hearings, counsel, impartiality, emergency procedures, appeals, and post-deprivation remedies.
functions.technologyLens: Service systems, calendars, remote hearings, case portals, language/accessibility tools, queueing, and transcript/record systems.
functions.fundingLens: Are hearing capacity, clerks, interpreters, counsel, record access, and appeals funded in proportion to caseload and stakes?
functions.evidence: Notice generation and delivery, access barriers, response opportunity, accommodations, decision reasons, and review disposition.
failureModes: Attempted notice treated as received notice
A deadline runs while access is blocked
Appeal exists on paper but not in practice

functions.name: Exercise agency without coercion
functions.purpose: Support informed choice, bodily autonomy, privacy, refusal, self-direction, and freedom from retaliation or coercive control.
functions.minimumTest: Can the person choose, refuse, seek advice, and change course without hidden penalties or a system treating compliance as consent?
functions.relationshipTest: Are power differences, dependency, age, disability, money, and safety accounted for without erasing the person’s agency?
functions.lawLens: Map consent, bodily autonomy, speech, religion, privacy, disability, labor, family, and anti-coercion protections.
functions.technologyLens: Consent interfaces, defaults, surveillance, account permissions, recommender systems, data sharing, and automated enforcement.
functions.fundingLens: Do incentives reward informed support and voluntary participation, or enrollment, compliance, and measurable conversion?
functions.evidence: Consent language, choice architecture, refusal, coercion indicators, data uses, and consequences.
failureModes: Click-through treated as informed consent
Safety justification used without necessity or expiry
Opt-out exists but is practically inaccessible

functions.name: Access opportunity and participation
functions.purpose: Enable education, work, housing, health, benefits, civic participation, culture, and meaningful inclusion.
functions.minimumTest: Can the person or group reach the opportunity, understand the criteria, compete fairly, and challenge exclusion with outcome data available?
functions.relationshipTest: Are opportunities distributed without requiring a person to abandon family, culture, disability needs, or caregiving responsibilities?
functions.lawLens: Map equal protection, civil rights, education, labor, housing, public benefits, voting, and public-access rules.
functions.technologyLens: Eligibility scoring, hiring and admissions systems, scheduling, digital identity, geofencing, and accessibility.
functions.fundingLens: Which outcomes receive appropriations, grants, reimbursements, tax incentives, or contracts—and who is left outside the denominator?
functions.evidence: Eligibility criteria, denominator, decisions, disparate impact signals, accessibility, appeals, and outcomes.
failureModes: Administrative convenience becomes exclusion
Success measured only among people who reached the system
Funding rewards visible outputs while externalizing access costs

functions.name: Coordinate care without losing context
functions.purpose: Preserve continuity across institutions, handoffs, professions, and households while keeping responsibility visible.
functions.minimumTest: When information or responsibility moves, can the receiving actor see what was known, what was uncertain, what authority transferred, and what must happen next?
functions.relationshipTest: Do handoffs preserve the person’s relationships and preferences instead of reducing them to a transferable case number?
functions.lawLens: Map interagency duties, confidentiality, mandated reporting, records transfer, professional scope, and accountability for missed handoffs.
functions.technologyLens: APIs, shared identifiers, referrals, data warehouses, interoperability, task queues, and notification systems.
functions.fundingLens: Are coordination and follow-up funded, or is each organization paid only for its own completed transaction?
functions.evidence: Lineage, handoff receipt, responsible actor, unresolved items, escalation, and closure reason.
failureModes: Context lost at the boundary
No one owns an unresolved task
Duplicate records create contradictory realities

functions.name: Protect privacy, security, and dignity
functions.purpose: Prevent unauthorized exposure, manipulation, surveillance, stigma, and use of personal data outside a legitimate purpose.
functions.minimumTest: Is collection necessary, access limited, use explained, security tested, retention bounded, and the person able to discover and challenge harmful processing?
functions.relationshipTest: Does confidentiality protect a person without blocking legitimate safety coordination or making family members jointly liable for one another’s data?
functions.lawLens: Map constitutional privacy, sector privacy laws, confidentiality, sealing, public-records exceptions, cybersecurity duties, and remedies.
functions.technologyLens: IAM, encryption, logging, data minimization, model training, vendor access, backups, and breach response.
functions.fundingLens: Are security, privacy engineering, audit, and incident response treated as funded operational functions rather than overhead to cut?
functions.evidence: Data inventory, purpose, access log, retention, control test, incident, notification, and remedy.
failureModes: Broad access justified by convenience
Data copied without purpose or expiry
Security treated as a purchase checkbox

functions.name: Learn, develop, and belong
functions.purpose: Support development, education, play, cultural identity, relationships, meaning, and participation across infancy, childhood, adulthood, and aging.
functions.minimumTest: Does the system account for developmental stage, culture, disability, and changing capacity while preserving connection and opportunities to learn?
functions.relationshipTest: Can the person remain connected to safe family, peers, mentors, community, and culture while gaining appropriate autonomy?
functions.lawLens: Map education, disability, child-development, elder services, cultural and religious protections, and public participation.
functions.technologyLens: Student information systems, learning platforms, care plans, recommendation systems, age gates, and social communication tools.
functions.fundingLens: Are long-term development and belonging funded, or only crisis response and short-term measurable outputs?
functions.evidence: Developmental context, preferences, participation, access, outcomes, and person or family feedback.
failureModes: Age label substitutes for individual assessment
Engagement metric substitutes for well-being
Cultural connection omitted from the record

functions.name: Repair error, restore trust, and sustain the future
functions.purpose: Make correction, appeal, reconciliation, compensation, learning, and intergenerational sustainability normal system functions.
functions.minimumTest: Can a person reverse a wrong record or decision, obtain a reasoned remedy, learn what failed, and prevent recurrence without retaliation?
functions.relationshipTest: Does repair restore safe relationships where possible and protect people where it is not, without forcing reconciliation?
functions.lawLens: Map correction, reconsideration, appeal, judicial review, complaints, compensation, records amendment, environmental and intergenerational duties.
functions.technologyLens: Correction workflows, immutable audit trails, incident management, model monitoring, versioning, and public dashboards.
functions.fundingLens: Is money allocated for appeals, independent oversight, remediation, maintenance, and prevention—not only initial delivery?
functions.evidence: Original state, error report, investigation, correction, outcome, recurrence analysis, and public accountability.
failureModes: Correction changes the visible record but not downstream copies
Appeal is counted as closure
No budget or owner exists for repair

fundingQuestions: What human function and relationship is the money intended to support?
What is purchased: a service, a decision, a data system, a throughput target, or an outcome?
What metric triggers payment, and what important harm or unmet need is outside the denominator?
Who can see the appropriation, grant, contract, vendor, subcontract, and performance report?
Who bears the risk when the funded system is wrong, delayed, inaccessible, or insecure?
Is correction, independent review, maintenance, and recovery funded as part of the function?

evidenceProtocol.label: Law
evidenceProtocol.text: Constitution, statute, rule, regulation, contract, or official policy; record the jurisdiction, version, and date.

evidenceProtocol.label: Norm
evidenceProtocol.text: Published standard, professional expectation, community value, or observed practice; label it as normative rather than binding law.

evidenceProtocol.label: Technology
evidenceProtocol.text: Actual interface, data model, workflow, access log, vendor documentation, outage, or observed system behavior.

evidenceProtocol.label: Funding
evidenceProtocol.text: Appropriation, award, contract, reimbursement, fee, performance measure, and recipient; trace the public dollars and obligations.

evidenceProtocol.label: Lived outcome
evidenceProtocol.text: What happened to a person or relationship; preserve source, context, challenge, and scope instead of generalizing one case.
